documents.title: University Guidelines for AI Use in the Classroom (provost announcement)
documents.summary: A December 2025 Provost announcement of UMBC's advisory guidelines for AI in the classroom. It leaves the decision to each instructor, offers a green/yellow/red traffic-light model and asks only for a clear syllabus statement. The full guidelines were not retrievable.
documents.stance_why: The announcement says "these guidelines are not a policy" and "Faculty retain full discretion to determine whether, how, and when AI tools are used in their courses"; it offers a traffic-light model for instructors to apply, so the document sets no stance itself and delegates.

units.why: The announcement says the guidelines "are not a policy" but "a shared framework"; this scopes the whole document as an advisory framework for AI in teaching, so it is P56 (framework statement), informs, general phase, neutral stance.
units.anchor: these guidelines are not a policy
units.frag_end: navigating the use of AI in teaching and learning
units.policy: The guidelines are not a policy; they are a shared framework to support faculty decision making on AI in teaching and learning.
units.fit_note: Also says the guidelines are explicitly advisory, not a policy.

units.why: "Faculty retain full discretion to determine whether, how, and when AI tools are used in their courses" hands the decision to each instructor, so it is P04, addressed to instructors, before-course, may.
units.anchor: Faculty retain full discretion to determine whether, how, and when AI tools are used

units.why: "We ask only that instructors clearly communicate their expectations regarding AI use in course syllabi" is the single duty placed on instructors, a syllabus-statement requirement (P09) at course start; coded must because it is the one thing asked.
units.anchor: clearly communicate their expectations regarding AI use in course syllabi

units.why: The guidelines "feature the 'traffic light' model (green, yellow, red)" to articulate "permissible, limited, or prohibited uses"; named color levels fit P05, and as the model is offered as a tool the modality is informs.
units.policy: The guidelines feature a traffic light model (green, yellow, red) to help instructors articulate permissible, limited, or prohibited uses of AI tools, particularly generative AI tools, within individual courses.

units.why: The Academic Integrity principle says "Faculty should clearly define expectations for AI use in assignments so students understand what is permitted"; this is a duty to state expectations, closest to P09 (statements in syllabus or assignment) rather than P66, since it requires no reasons to be given.
units.anchor: Faculty should clearly define expectations for AI use in assignments

units.why: The same principle wants students to understand "what constitutes academic dishonesty", tying AI rules to integrity; P36 is nearest but the text does not say unauthorized use is misconduct, only that expectations separate permitted use from dishonesty.
units.frag_start: so students understand what is permitted
units.policy: Students are to understand what AI use is permitted and what constitutes academic dishonesty.
units.fit_note: Does not state outright that unauthorized AI use is misconduct.

units.why: The Pedagogical Choice principle says faculty "align AI use with course learning objectives and disciplinary norms"; the alignment criterion makes this P83, not just P04.
units.anchor: align AI use with course learning objectives and disciplinary norms

units.why: The same principle calls the traffic light model "a decision support tool", so the tiers are optional help, not a mandated scheme; coded P05 with a note.
units.anchor: using the traffic light model as a decision support tool
units.fit_note: The tiers are advisory decision support, not a required scheme.

units.why: The Responsible Use principle says "All users are expected to engage with AI tools ethically, with attention to data privacy, intellectual property, and institutional policies"; it binds everyone to ethics, privacy, IP and existing policy. P77 (follow existing policy) fits best; P50 does not because no concrete data protection is stated.
units.anchor: expected to engage with AI tools ethically, with attention to data privacy
units.fit_note: Also names ethical use, data privacy and intellectual property as concerns, which P77 does not capture.

units.why: The action item "Include a clear statement on AI use for the upcoming term" directs instructors to put an AI statement in their syllabi, which is P09, at course start.
units.anchor: Include a clear statement on AI use for the upcoming term

units.why: "Sample language and templates are provided in the guidelines document" is a support the institution supplies for syllabus statements; no type covers provided templates, so UNCOVERED rather than a stretch to P09.
units.anchor: Sample language and templates are provided in the guidelines document
units.policy: Sample language and templates for syllabus AI statements are provided in the guidelines document.
units.uncovered_note: The institution supplies sample syllabus language and templates to help instructors write AI statements.

units.why: "We welcome ongoing feedback as questions, concerns, and effective practices emerge" invites feedback on the guidelines, which is P54 (feedback invited).
units.anchor: We welcome ongoing feedback as questions, concerns, and effective practices emerge

units.why: "we will continue to update them based on technological advancements and community feedback" commits the university to revising the guidelines, a P54 revisit commitment.
units.anchor: we will continue to update them based on technological advancements and community feedback

units.why: "developed through broad consultation between faculty and staff and reflect emerging best practices and examples from peer institutions" describes how the guidelines were made, which is P84.
units.anchor: developed through broad consultation between faculty and staff

units.why: "we are also sharing links to resources within the guidelines document, including how other universities have handled this challenge" points faculty to peer practice; P88 (peers) is nearest, though it is a resource list.
units.anchor: how other universities have handled this challenge
units.frag_start: Given that we are a community
units.fit_note: Offers resource links to faculty, not coalitions or partnerships.

units.why: The guidelines are for AI tools "in the classroom and in academic administration", fixing their scope; P56 (framework scope) fits, and P76 does not because no administrative rule is stated here.
units.anchor: in the classroom and in academic administration

units.why: The action item "Review the Full Guidelines" asks instructors to read the guidelines document; P102 (stay informed) is nearest but it concerns the guidance itself rather than AI developments.
units.policy: Instructors review the full guidelines document.
units.fit_note: Asks for review of the guidelines document itself, not of AI developments generally.

notes: Only the Provost announcement was coded; the full guidelines file is behind my.UMBC login. Summary-level text, so the unit count is small.
